scope: Independent full-viewport visual review of native iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 synthetic captures. Screenshots only; no Simulator interaction, implementation inspection, other reviews, or plans were used.

categories.strength: At default size, topics and names lead; operational review text and recency occupy a lower level. The synthetic label is quiet and sparse lists remain honestly sparse.
Default-size titles, context, and timestamps are comfortably distinct in both themes. AX5 text enlarges visibly instead of using tiny metadata.
Default rows use coherent text baselines, quiet separators, and balanced vertical spacing; the single filtered result does not acquire filler.
Warm neutral fields, restrained separators, and scarce review color support the content. The unread session alone gains a surface; read rows remain flat, without redundant chevrons.
Both pages share search/filter placement, navigation treatment, and composer. The active filter shows its scope and an explicit reset glyph. Chinese dark chrome retains the same structure.

evidence: 07-sessions-ax5.png: count and Synthetic preview block above the first topic
08-people-ax5.png: count and Synthetic preview block above the first identity
deductions.observation: At AX5, utility metadata becomes a broad two-line heading nearly as forceful as the content. The first topic/name begins around two-fifths down the full viewport.
deductions.basis: Observed layout; the deduction is for utility prominence, not for allowing large text to scroll.

deductions.observation: Leila's identity leads the context line before the search, while Nia's identity is below the search in smaller footer text. The person-to-conversation association changes its scan position between adjacent rows.
deductions.basis: Observed hierarchy inconsistency; both identities remain readable.

evidence: 07-sessions-ax5.png: top tabs read Today, Ses..., Peo...
08-people-ax5.png: top tabs read Today, Ses..., Peo...
deductions.observation: Two destination labels truncate at the largest tested size, including the selected page label.
deductions.basis: Observed text loss; accessible names and alternatives were not inspected.

evidence: 08-people-ax5.png: first identity reads Leila / Hart- / mann
deductions.observation: The surname is split with a visible hyphen across two lines, making a single identity harder to read as a unit.
deductions.basis: Observed line breaking; the complete name is present, so this is not a claim of lost identity data.

deductions.observation: The one-result state says '1 people' instead of '1 person'.

evidence: 08-people-ax5.png: avatar beside the middle name line; role returns to the outer row inset
deductions.observation: The retained avatar column narrows the name into a tall block, centers the avatar beside its middle, then resets role/company text to the outer inset. The identity and context form a visibly staggered group.
deductions.basis: Observed grouping and alignment issue; does not penalize vertical scrolling or sparse data.

evidence: 07-sessions-ax5.png: elevated bottom composer and enlarged plus/waveform
08-people-ax5.png: elevated bottom composer and enlarged plus/waveform
deductions.observation: The tinted, shadowed composer expands into a dominant bottom object, with very large nontext symbols. Its material and glyph weight compete with retrieval content.
deductions.basis: Subjective material judgment tied to visible full-viewport competition; readable accessible text should be preserved.

deductions.observation: The shared shell retains its default horizontal layout after destination names no longer fit. Navigation therefore loses its complete visual labels at a supported text size.
deductions.basis: Distinct system-adaptation consequence of the truncation recorded in T1; no tap or VoiceOver failure is claimed.

evidence: 07-sessions-ax5.png: first session menu remains beside the topic
08-people-ax5.png: no corresponding menu is visible beside the first identity
deductions.observation: The first People row does not retain a visible secondary menu near its identity in this AX5 viewport, although the Sessions menu remains near the topic.
deductions.basis: Observed first-viewport inconsistency only; the menu may be reachable after scrolling or by another mechanism, which these captures cannot establish.

corrections.correction: Give the shared shell an accessibility-size composition: keep full destination names, demote the count/preview block without shrinking accessible text, and reduce the composer's decorative and symbol weight while preserving its functions.
corrections.verification: Recapture both full AX5 viewports with all destination names visible; directly inspect navigation, composer content access, actual command targets, and VoiceOver. Do not treat screenshot improvement as functional proof.

corrections.correction: Reflow People identity at accessibility sizes so the name can use the row width, avatar/name/context form a coherent vertical group, and the secondary menu stays visibly associated with that person.
corrections.verification: Capture long names at AX5 and confirm Hartmann remains an intact word where available width permits; inspect the menu and all lower row content through direct scrolling and accessibility traversal.

corrections.correction: Use correct singular/plural English result labels for filtered People counts.
corrections.verification: Check zero-, one-, and two-result labels; the one-result capture must read '1 person'.

missing_proof: Search and filter execution on both pages, including resetting empty results.
Read/unread transitions and persistence; the still-image surface difference does not establish semantics.
Actual 44-point command hit regions, page navigation, menu access, and all content access at AX5.
Identity/provenance integrity and absence of unexpected external writes.
VoiceOver names/order, contrast measurements, keyboard/focus behavior, interruption, and recovery.

interpretation: 80/100 is a subjective craft judgment across all eight uncropped views, not measured preference, a reviewer average, or release approval. Default-size craft is stronger than the visible AX5 shell and identity layout.
